source.manufacturer: Chalmers University of Technology, Department of Industrial and Materials Science (MSc thesis, Sofia Dahl, 2023; supervisor Stefan Pierrau, Scania CV AB; examiner Dag Henrik Bergsjo)
source.document_id: 'Implementing ISO 26262-5 - A guide to Functional Safety for Product Development at Hardware Level', sections 4.4.2-4.4.4 (SPFM, LFM, PMHF equations) and 4.5 / 5.3.2 (worked example totals and results)

note: H-09 (issue #56) second tool-qualification fixture for tools/fmeda-calculator.py (OR-004). The thesis works an FMEDA example that the author states is 'based on an example provided in ISO 26262-5' (ASIL C safety goal 'Avoid unintended drive off', function 'Gearbox must be in neutral'; 1 ECU, 5 resistors, 2 inductors, 3 capacitors). Only the aggregate sums and results are available as text (the per-component Table 5 is an image), so this fixture exercises the metric equations from the sums: SPFM = 1 - 6.9055/127 = 94.56 %, LFM = 1 - 7.4/(127 - 6.9055) = 93.84 %, PMHF = 6.9055 + 7.4 x 76.372 x 1e5/1e9 = 6.9620 FIT with T_lifetime = 100 000 h, reproduced exactly by the calculator at the thesis precision. The thesis result is itself an honest failure (SPFM 94.56 % < 97 % ASIL C target) and is used verbatim. No PDF is retained; source_url is the university repository.
